name: Haile Selassie I
summary: Haile Selassie ruled Ethiopia personally for nearly six decades as a hereditary, divinely anointed emperor, granting constitutions in 1931 and 1955 that kept sovereignty in his own hands while creating a partly elected Parliament. He pursued top-down modernization through education, planning and foreign capital, centralized the state (including the 1962 annexation of Eritrea), and defended the Orthodox Church as the established church. Abroad he championed collective security, the UN, disarmament, African unity and the end of colonialism and racial discrimination, and kept Ethiopia formally non-aligned.

free-trade.rationale: Told a US business audience that impediments to the free flow of international trade and preferential tariffs hold back developing countries and urged the advanced nations to waive them.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Called planning indispensable for the rational use of capital and aid and said scarce resources should go to a carefully selected list of priorities; his Five-Year Plans stressed primary industries, power and roads.

property-fundamental.rationale: His constitution guarantees the right to own and dispose of property, allowing expropriation only by law with just compensation, and his investment decree protects investors from arbitrary expropriation.

national-resource-control.rationale: His constitution makes subsoil resources and forests State Domain to be exploited only under imperial conservation law, while he invited foreign firms to exploit them as partners of the state.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Praised self-help but actively sought foreign aid, credits and private capital from both East and West and told Americans Ethiopia wanted more investment, so he did not hold that a poor country should rely only on itself.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Told a US audience that the developed nations have a responsibility to make their capital and technology available to poor countries and that the gap between rich and poor must not be allowed to continue.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for removal of outmoded international arrangements that handicap developing countries, remunerative guaranteed prices for primary goods, waiver of preferential tariffs and implementation of the UNCTAD recommendations.

delink-world-market.rationale: Argued that developing nations should attract foreign capital and skills and that all peoples are economically interdependent, the opposite of breaking ties with rich countries.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Stressed the essential interdependence of all peoples in economic life and the mutual benefit of co-operative economic effort, which is incompatible with a shut-off self-sufficient bloc.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said outmoded international trade arrangements seriously limit developing countries, and described colonial Africa as a resource to be exploited and a market for others' goods.

future-generations.rationale: His constitution declares the waters, forests, land and other natural resources a sacred trust for present and succeeding generations and orders their conservation.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said freedom and the rights of man mean little to the ignorant, hungry, ill-clothed and badly housed, and that people need education and minimum economic security to take part in national life.

unions-good.rationale: His government allowed labour unions in 1962 but restricted their activity; he left no statement of his own on whether unions are good, so the record is mixed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Welcomed science and modernization but said civilization serves good or evil purposes depending on moral guidance and that progress without religion is dangerous.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Said modern civilization and science have greatly improved man's life and brought comfort, while warning they can be misused.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Ruled as hereditary emperor for 44 years; his constitution vests all sovereignty in the Emperor and attaches the imperial dignity perpetually to his line.

sacred-ruler.rationale: His constitution declares the Emperor's person sacred by imperial blood and anointing, descended from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, his dignity inviolable and his powers indisputable.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Wrote into the constitution that the imperial dignity stays in his line with succession by his male descendants.

elective-rulers.rationale: His constitution provides for lineal male succession, with no election of the ruler.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: His constitution makes the head of state hereditary rather than elected by anyone.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: His constitution entrenches the imperial line and gives the Emperor sole power to confer the title of Prince and other honours.

parliament-supreme.rationale: His constitution vests supreme authority in the Emperor, who initiates laws, may return them, dissolve the chambers and appoints the Senate.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Grounded his authority in blood, anointing and election by God, not in the consent of the governed.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: His title and constitution call him elect of God and rest the Emperor's powers on anointing, and he told judges that kings received their mission from God.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution bars suits against the Emperor and makes his person inviolable, yet he swore to govern by the constitution and laws and told judges rulers must not deviate from the law.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: His constitution makes the Emperor inviolable, bars suits against him and punishes anyone who seeks to injure him, with no right to remove him.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The constitution makes him commander-in-chief with sole power to appoint and dismiss the Prime Minister and all ministers.

second-chamber.rationale: His constitutions created a bicameral Parliament, an elected Chamber of Deputies alongside an appointed Senate.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: His constitution requires the budget to be voted item by item by Parliament and bars spending not authorised by law, though Parliament may not raise the total.

term-limits.rationale: His constitution makes deputies eligible for re-election with no limit and allows senators to be reappointed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Prepared the revised constitution himself and proclaimed it by decree; the Library of Congress study says Parliament played no part in drawing it up.

separated-powers.rationale: His constitution gives the courts nominal independence but vests supreme authority over all branches in the Emperor, who appoints ministers, senators and judges.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He granted a chapter of rights that needs a three-quarters vote in both chambers and his approval to amend, but the same text qualifies them by law and the guarantees were largely unrealised in practice.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His constitution lets the Emperor declare a state of siege, martial law or national emergency, censor correspondence and issue emergency decrees.

conscription.rationale: His constitution makes military service a duty of every subject when called upon.

decide-locally.rationale: Centralized local government under governors-general he appointed and appointed municipal mayors from short lists; the Library of Congress study describes his drive to put local government in the central administration's hands.

right-to-secede.rationale: His constitution declares the empire's sovereignty and territory indivisible and he ended Eritrea's federal status in 1962.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Held the empire indivisible, urged states such as Sudan to preserve their unity and territorial integrity, and imperial forces fought the Eritrean separatists under his rule.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Accepted Eritrea's federation with its own government in 1952 and autonomy for the Afar sultan, but then dismantled Eritrea's autonomy.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Granted autonomy to the Afar sultan and accepted Eritrea's federal status, welcomed regional autonomy for southern Sudan, yet centralized the state and warned against fragmentation along tribal lines.

native-born-offices.rationale: His constitution requires ministers' parents to have been Ethiopian subjects and deputies and senators to be Ethiopian by birth.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Spoke for tolerance of dissent in a speech, but the record shows parties proscribed in Eritrea and the 1960 coup attempt put down.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Laws were published in the Negarit Gazeta and judges were told to follow the law, but the Emperor also ruled by decree and personally heard appeals.

democracy-best.rationale: Said an educated people is needed for representative and democratic organs of government and extended an elected chamber, but kept sovereignty in his own hands.

state-harmful.rationale: His constitution makes the state, headed by the Emperor, responsible for defence, the safety and welfare of inhabitants and their rights.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His constitution charges the Emperor with the welfare of subjects and his government built schools, hospitals, universities and development plans.

taxation-theft.rationale: His constitution regulates taxes by law and he decreed a land tax system in 1942 and pushed land-tax reform in the 1960s.

private-courts-defense.rationale: His constitution makes justice, defence and security the Emperor's right and duty, administered through state courts and armed forces.

death-penalty.rationale: His constitution keeps capital punishment and requires the Emperor to confirm every death sentence.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: His constitution makes everyone's duty to respect and obey the constitution, laws, decrees and orders explicit.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Told judges that where a specific law exists they must try according to the law.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said all men are born equal and must be equal before the law, wrote equal protection and non-discrimination into his constitution, and spoke for the equality of man at the UN, while keeping an imperial hierarchy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Made the Ethiopian Orthodox Church the established church supported by the State, required the Emperor to profess it and mention his name in all services.

national-church-status.rationale: His constitution makes the Ethiopian Orthodox Church the Established Church of the Empire, supported by the State.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: His constitution gives one church, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, established status in law.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said progress without religion is like a body without a soul and that one must be guided by religion; his constitution makes the Orthodox faith the Emperor's duty.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Brought church land under taxation, removed clergy's own courts over civil offences and took the appointment of the abun, while still supporting the church.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: His constitution forbids using religious rites for political purposes and religious organizations for commercial purposes.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Said kings judged by the Fetha Negest and respected it, but also drove modern civil and criminal codes and guaranteed freedom of religious rites.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said faith in the Almighty sustained him, that one needs faith in God, and urged secular learning as a path to recognizing a Creator.

religion-illusion.rationale: Held religion essential to a good life and civilization, calling progress without religion a body without a soul.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Established the Orthodox Church and professed Christianity, and spoke for religion as the guide of progress.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Told judges that man cannot live on bread alone and has a spirit to care for, and his coronation oath pledges the spiritual and material welfare of subjects.

traditional-family.rationale: His constitution calls the family the source of the maintenance and development of the empire and the primary basis of education and social harmony, under special legal protection.

women-suffrage.rationale: His revised constitution gives all Ethiopian subjects aged 21 the right to vote and be elected and bars discrimination in civil rights; succession alone is male.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Restricted the throne to men but told the nation that women worldwide want civic roles beyond housekeeping and urged girls' schooling.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Condemned apartheid and racial segregation at the UN and OAU as an affront to human dignity.

racial-franchise.rationale: His constitution grants the vote to all Ethiopian subjects without racial or ethnic limits, and he demanded equal human rights for all regardless of race.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Declared that Africans possess all human attributes and talents no more and no less than others and that the philosophy of one race being superior and another inferior must be abandoned.

racial-pride.rationale: Urged Africans to be proud of their own special qualities, distinctions and abilities.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Backed President Kennedy's drive to remove the remaining vestiges of racial discrimination and called for ending exploitation of one people by another.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Said civilizations that flourished in Africa suffer not at all by comparison with those of other continents and mocked others' conceit that the world ended at their horizons.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Told students Ethiopia has its own cultures and mores, characteristics of Ethiopianness, and said he does not want the legacies and traditions lost.

gradual-change.rationale: Said African union can come only gradually and compromised in practice with the nobility on social reform.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said differences of race, religion and culture are no insuperable obstacle to unity, but warned that tribalism and tribal division weaken nations.

single-official-language.rationale: His constitution makes Amharic the official language and he made Amharic official in Eritrea in place of Arabic and Tigrinya.

minority-language-support.rationale: Made Amharic the official language, displacing Arabic and Tigrinya in Eritrea.

patriotic-education.rationale: Told graduates to be unswerving in their loyalty to their country and said education is the way to maintain the unity of Ethiopians.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: His constitution traces the dynasty without interruption to Menelik I, and he spoke of Ethiopia as a state of three thousand years.

leader-cult.rationale: Redirected a statue proposed in his honour into a university, but his constitution orders his name mentioned in all religious services.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Urged Ethiopians not to repay evil for evil after the Italian occupation and told Africans to forswear recrimination and vengeance against former colonizers.

revolution-justified.rationale: Backed armed African liberation movements and told the UN Africans will fight if necessary, though he condemned the 1960 coup attempt.

political-violence-never.rationale: Supported aid to African freedom fighters through the OAU Liberation Committee, so he did not hold political violence never justified.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said a non-aligned state judges policies by their worth, not by their source or sponsor, and that ideologies need not divide nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Condemned narrow self-interest and malicious inhuman self-interest as obstacles to peace and unity, speaking of nations.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the UN that its executive must have greater authority and the means to enforce its decisions, and said earlier that it needs its own strong force.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said the ultimate destiny of Africa lies in political union and told the UN that salvation rests in subordinating national interests to the interests of mankind.

nation-first.rationale: Told the UN that men must be persuaded to subordinate national interests to mankind's and warned Africans against narrow self-interest.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called disarmament the urgent imperative of our time and supported the nuclear test ban, while saying nations need defence.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said no nation can afford to neglect its basic defence requirements and built up Ethiopia's forces.

collective-defense.rationale: Made collective security the central cause of his foreign policy and urged an African defence system giving speedy aid to any state threatened with aggression.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said every nation has an inherent right to shape its own destiny and backed the independence of colonized African peoples, while ending Eritrea's autonomy and resisting Somali claims.

non-intervention.rationale: Held that interference in another country's internal affairs breaks the UN Charter and stressed non-interference as a principle applied uniformly, though he supported UN collective action.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Declared Ethiopia non-aligned by its own choice and defined non-alignment at Belgrade, yet took US military aid.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Kept a military assistance and mutual security relationship with the United States and sent troops to Korea and the Congo.

dominated-front.rationale: Told non-aligned states they are not a power bloc and must not attack either side unjustifiably.

defeat-communism.rationale: Said nations of differing ideologies can live side by side, visited the Soviet Union and accepted Soviet aid.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemned colonialism as reducing Africans to humiliation and slavery and exploiting them.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Described colonial Africa as a physical resource to be exploited and a market for others' goods and condemned it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Sent Ethiopian troops to Korea and the Congo under collective security rather than only to defend Ethiopia.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Called colonial boundaries artificial and arbitrary but treated the unity and territorial integrity of existing states as paramount for Africa and for Sudan.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pursued Eritrea's return, citing a 'lost' territory regained by peaceful means, and in 1945 claimed Italian Somaliland as a lost province.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Called Eritrea a territory torn from the Motherland and restored, but opposed Somali unification across the Ethiopian border.

national-law-over-international.rationale: His constitution declares the constitution together with Ethiopia's international treaties the supreme law of the empire.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Denounced a secret agreement of January 1935 as a violation of the Covenant that abandoned Ethiopia.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: His government abandoned the Christian-Muslim parity in Eritrean offices.

notes: Evidence is his own constitution, speeches and interviews and the record of his rule; Rastafari beliefs about him are not his positions. The imperial press translations of speeches are hosted on Wikisource and cited as mirrors of the originals. Not available: his autobiography 'My Life and Ethiopia's Progress' (archive.org lending copy only, borrow-restricted), the 1931 constitution full text, and his land-reform and Eritrea 1962 speeches, so land redistribution and Eritrean self-determination rest on scholarly accounts or are null. The 1955 constitution is treated as his own measure (he states he prepared it; the Library of Congress study says Parliament played no part in drawing it up), but its rights chapter is weighed against the record that the guarantees were largely unrealised. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means. Most economy (taxes, welfare, labour, housing), personal-liberty (drugs, sex, guns), gender and identity, ideology-specific and technology statements are null because he said nothing on them in the sources reached.
